tools.name: metaform_view
tools.description: Read the functional namespace or focused knowledge through one of the three required views. Local reads preserve direct incoming/outgoing functional relationships without dumping neighbor knowledge. Read only.

project.description: Optional project selection; otherwise use the current chassis project context.

address.description: Exact project-relative functional namespace address. Do not transform its segments.

cursor.description: Continuation returned by this read, not a namespace property.

namespace.description: Native nested namespace projection. This envelope field is not stored as another namespace wrapper.

receivers.description: Derived direct reverse relationships for a local focus; not additional stored copies.

address.description: Exact project-relative functional namespace address. Do not transform its segments.

revision.description: Read-result version supplied by the service, not a new field on each element.

cursor.description: Null means this projection is complete; otherwise continue the same read.

NamespaceValue.title: Value at a namespace address
NamespaceValue.description: Objects extend the addressed hierarchy or hold structured data. Arrays denote composed element layers; scalars are direct values.

NamespaceNode.title: Namespace branch or receiving element
NamespaceNode.description: Namespace branch or receiving element. Its properties and layers are directly on the element. The same word can name metadata or a namespace branch according to its value and context.

anyOf.description: The name used for this functionality in project documentation or specifications, such as Metaform.
Functional role at the examined scope. DE is the Defining Element: without this functionality the artifact can no longer be the same kind of thing.

Implementation state. Use un_built for intended functionality not yet built. Legacy not_built/missing/todo spellings and intake BKN/broken judgments are not accepted. Other lifecycle state names are not defined by this schema.
Number of trailing namespace segments, including the leaf, read backward to form the accepted industry technical name. Count segments, not words.

providers.description: An array is the functional knowledge layer. An object is a namespace branch and follows namespace rules.

op.description: A namespace branch or native layer can use this word. The scalar encounter field belongs in a provider relationship, not on the namespace node.

ef.description: A namespace branch or native layer can use this word. The scalar encounter field belongs in a provider relationship, not on the namespace node.

anyOf.description: Optional project metadata; does not introduce a required wrapper.

propertyNames.description: One namespace segment, never a dotted reference or JSONPath expression.

ComposedElementLayer.title: Array-valued composed element layer
ComposedElementLayer.description: An array at a plural-named namespace location is a knowledge layer. Its members retain their native formats and nesting. Do not reinterpret fields inside native members as functional namespace branches.

Providers.title: Functional knowledge layer
Providers.description: Provider relationships owned by this receiving element. Address keys reference elements in the tree. Properties of those elements remain at their tree locations. No ordering meaning is imposed.

propertyNames.description: Project-relative reference to an element in the actual nested namespace.

ProviderRecord.title: Provider record
ProviderRecord.description: Receiver-owned relationship fields: OP is why this RE needs the provider; EF is how that PE serves this RE. One relationship per provider address within its receiver. The PE address is a reference, not a location for the PE's properties.

ice.description: Indicates indivisible coupling in the receiving/provider relationship. This boolean is not information-flow direction or a generated Block ID.

ifd.description: Direction of the substance that satisfies this RE's OP: send, receive or both, relative to the receiver. Excludes request and parameter traffic. These literals follow the owner-supplied schema; historical sends/receives spellings are not silently accepted.

op.description: The active goal (why) of the Receiving Entity (RE) that the EF must satisfy. Formatted strictly in ASD-STE100.

ef.description: The mechanism, interface, relationship, or method of the provider that satisfies the op. Formatted strictly in ASD-STE100.

tools.name: metaform_apply
tools.description: Apply a coherent batch of native namespace changes and explicit removals. Use receiver-owned providers arrays keyed by provider addresses; referenced elements remain in the tree. No SQL, Cypher, row IDs or one call per attribute. Mutation semantics in this packet are proposals for owner review.

project.description: Optional project selection; otherwise use the current chassis project context.

changes.description: A coherent partial namespace in the confirmed native tree shape; may contain multiple receivers and their providers arrays.

layer_mode.description: Proposed explicit append/replace behavior for supplied ancillary native arrays; does not change provider address identity. Safe omission behavior and mixed per-layer updates must be finalized before implementation.

expected_revision.description: Proposed observed project revision precondition; service checks it atomically.

operation_id.description: Proposed retry identity scoped by authenticated caller and selected project. Same key with different content is an error.
